hero.eyebrow: Arcana Subclass · XIV · Temperance · Aspect of Empathy

epigraph.html: We feel what you feel before you do, and the Weave lets us turn it into something else.

hero.ledeHtml: Mystra wove the Heartweaver from the feelings that pass between every living thing, a thread that tempers one emotion with another. They surge joy, trust or fear into a creature's Weave, then braid what lingers into stronger feelings that lift allies and break enemies from within. The Heartweaver deals little damage of their own. They win by deciding what everyone on the field feels, and in what order: a surge now, a mood that lingers, and a second surge that turns the two into something stronger.

blocks.html:
Temperance is the fourteenth card of the Major Arcana. It shows a winged figure with one foot in a stream and one on dry land, pouring water from one cup into another. The stream runs at an angle no water should follow, and not a drop is spilled. Nothing is added and nothing is lost: the two cups simply trade what they hold until they balance.

The card stands for moderation, patience and the art of blending. It is the alchemist's card, the slow work of mixing two things until they become a third. It follows Death in the Major Arcana, and its lesson is what comes after an ending: mixing again, gently, until the measure is right.

That is the Heartweaver's destiny. They do not create feelings out of nothing. They pour one emotion into a creature that already holds another, and the two become something new. Joy poured into trust becomes Love. Fear poured into surprise becomes Awe. Pour a feeling into its opposite and the cup cracks.

upright.title: Upright
upright.html: Your allies feel the right thing at the right moment. Trust steadies them, joy sharpens them, and the feelings you braid from both carry them through the fight.

reversed.title: Reversed
reversed.html: Your enemies feel too much, all at once. Their emotions overflow into Terror and Grief, and opposites forced together snap into Catharsis.

blocks.html: The Heartweaver is a controller and a support caster. Each Weave Surge fills a creature with one emotion for a single turn. When that emotion fades it leaves a milder mood behind, and the next Surge you cast on that creature reacts with the mood instead of landing on its own. Your turns alternate between laying moods and spending them: freeze an enemy with Fear now, then turn its lingering apprehension into Awe or Despair. The same rules work on your allies, so a single Surge can shut an enemy down on one side of the field and lift a friend on the other.

blocks.title: At a Glance
blocks.html:
• Role: controller and support. Low damage, with spikes of Catharsis.
  • Strengths: strong control from level 1 spells, buffs and debuffs from the same spell, more targets with every slot level, and allies never need to roll against you.
  • Weaknesses: needs a turn of setup, enemies resist with Wisdom Saving Throws, and creatures with Intelligence 4 or lower feel nothing at all.
  • Tip: Surge an ally with Trust before the fight turns ugly. Next turn it is Accepting, and a Weave Surge: Joy braids it into Love.

rows.label: Hit Points
rows.html: 6 + your Constitution modifier at level 1, then 4 + your Constitution modifier per level

rows.label: Skills
rows.html: Choose 4 from Animal Handling, Insight, Intimidation, Medicine, Perception, Performance, Persuasion and Religion. Then gain Expertise in 2 of them.

rows.label: Suggested Abilities
rows.html: Strength 8, Dexterity 10, Constitution 10, Intelligence 15, Wisdom 15, Charisma 13, then +2 and +1 to the abilities of your choice

rows.label: Starting Equipment
rows.html: Leather Armour, a Dagger, Darts, 2 Potions of Healing, a Scroll of Revivify, an Alchemy Pouch, camp clothes and camp supplies

blocks.html:
Heartweavers teach that every feeling a mind can hold is spun from eight threads: Joy, Trust, Fear, Surprise, Sadness, Disgust, Anger and Anticipation. Laid out in a circle, each thread sits beside its closest kin and directly across from its opposite. Joy faces Sadness, Trust faces Disgust, Fear faces Anger, and Surprise faces Anticipation.

Every thread can be pulled gently or hard. Pulled gently, it becomes a mood, a soft echo that lingers. Pulled hard, it becomes overwhelming. Two threads that touch braid into a feeling, and the farther apart they sit, the stranger that feeling is.

Everything the Heartweaver does follows the same three steps.

  1. Surge. A Weave Surge fills a creature with one emotion for 1 turn, such as Emotion: Fear. This is the peak, and it is the strongest effect a single Surge has.
  2. Mood. When the emotion fades on its own, it leaves the milder echo of itself behind for 5 turns: Fear leaves the creature Apprehensive. If the emotion is removed early, it leaves no mood.
  3. Reaction. Cast another Weave Surge on a creature that carries a mood and the two threads react instead of surging. The mood is spent, and what you get depends on how far apart the two emotions sit on the wheel.

A creature feels one emotion at a time and carries one mood at a time; a new one replaces the old. Feelings are different: each one is its own thread, so a creature can carry several different feelings at once.

blocks.title: Every Weave Surge
blocks.html:
• Is a level 1 Enchantment spell cast as an action, with a range of 18m.
  • Touches one creature, plus one more for every slot level above 1: 3 creatures with a level 3 slot, 6 with a level 6 slot.
  • Can target any creature that carries a mood, friend or foe. A creature without a mood can only receive Joy, Trust and Anticipation if it is your ally (or you), and only Fear, Surprise, Sadness, Disgust and Anger if it is not.
  • Asks a Wisdom Saving Throw only of creatures that aren't your allies. Allies never roll.
  • Needs a mind to work on: creatures with Intelligence 4 or lower can't be targeted.
  • Lands as a plain emotion if its reaction isn't unlocked yet. The old mood stays until the new emotion fades and replaces it.

Find the Surge you cast on the left and the mood the creature carries along the top. A small number marks the level at which that reaction unlocks; reactions without one work from level 1. Overwhelming emotions are in italics.

features.name: Emotional Alchemy
features.bodyHtml:
When your Weave Surge touches a creature that already carries a mood, the threads react instead of surging, and the mood is spent.

Neighbouring emotions braid into a feeling, such as Love, that lasts 2 turns.

Opposing emotions snap into Catharsis: an enemy takes 2d8 Psychic damage and an ally regains 2d8 hit points.

See The Wheel of Emotions and the reaction chart.

features.name: Empathic Sight
features.bodyHtml:
You read the threads of feeling in others.

You have Advantage on Insight checks.

features.name: Weave Surge: Joy
features.bodyHtml:
Pluck a bright thread of joy in an ally's Weave.

The target has Advantage on Attack Rolls and Ability Checks. When the surge fades, it leaves the target Serene for 5 turns, with Advantage on Wisdom Saving Throws.

Reacts with: Accepting into Love, Interested into Optimism · Apprehensive into Guilt, Annoyed into Pride (level 5) · Distracted into Delight, Bored into Morbidness (level 9) · Pensive into Catharsis · Serene into Ecstasy (level 7).

At higher levels: one more target per slot level above 1, up to 6 targets with a level 6 slot.

features.name: Weave Surge: Trust
features.bodyHtml:
Steady an ally with a thread of trust.

The target gains a +2 bonus to Armour Class and has Advantage on Saving Throws. When the surge fades, it leaves the target Accepting for 5 turns, with a +1 bonus to Armour Class.

Reacts with: Serene into Love, Apprehensive into Submission · Distracted into Curiosity, Interested into Hope (level 5) · Pensive into Sentimentality, Annoyed into Dominance (level 9) · Bored into Catharsis · Accepting into Admiration (level 7).

At higher levels: one more target per slot level above 1, up to 6 targets with a level 6 slot.

features.name: Weave Surge: Fear
features.bodyHtml:
Wrap a creature in a cold thread of fear.

The target can't move and has Disadvantage on Ability Checks and Attack Rolls. When the surge fades, it leaves the target Apprehensive for 5 turns, subtracting 1d4 from its Wisdom Saving Throws.

Reacts with: Accepting into Submission, Distracted into Awe · Serene into Guilt, Pensive into Despair (level 5) · Bored into Shame, Interested into Anxiety (level 9) · Annoyed into Catharsis · Apprehensive into Terror (level 7).

At higher levels: one more target per slot level above 1, up to 6 targets with a level 6 slot.

features.name: Heartstring
features.bodyHtml:
Tug a single string of a creature's heart. The target takes 1d4 Psychic damage. If it carries a mood, the mood lasts 2 turns longer.

At higher levels: 2d4 Psychic at level 5 and 3d4 Psychic at level 10.

features.name: Read the Room
features.bodyHtml: Out of combat only. You have Advantage on Insight and Persuasion checks against a creature that isn't hostile to you.

features.name: 14 - Temperance: Awakening
features.bodyHtml:
Cause reactions with Emotional Alchemy during a fight to awaken the Aspect of Empathy until combat ends. Each goal you reach awakens one more tier.

Level 3: cause 3 reactions to gain Attunement. Level 7: cause 5 reactions to also gain Harmony. Level 12: cause 7 reactions to awaken as the Aspect of Empathy.

The tiers and what they grant are under Aspect of Empathy.

features.name: Weave Surge: Anticipation
features.bodyHtml:
Pull a taut thread of anticipation through an ally's Weave.

The target gains an additional reaction, and its movement speed is doubled. When the surge fades, it leaves the target Interested for 5 turns, with its movement speed increased by 3m.

Reacts with: Serene into Optimism, Annoyed into Aggressiveness · Accepting into Hope, Bored into Cynicism (level 5) · Apprehensive into Anxiety, Pensive into Pessimism (level 9) · Distracted into Catharsis · Interested into Vigilance (level 7).

At higher levels: one more target per slot level above 1, up to 6 targets with a level 6 slot.

features.name: Weave Surge: Surprise
features.bodyHtml:
Snap a thread of surprise before a creature's eyes.

The target can't take reactions or bonus actions and has Disadvantage on Dexterity Saving Throws. When the surge fades, it leaves the target Distracted for 5 turns, with Disadvantage on Saving Throws to maintain Concentration.

Reacts with: Apprehensive into Awe, Pensive into Disapproval · Accepting into Curiosity, Bored into Unbelief (level 5) · Serene into Delight, Annoyed into Outrage (level 9) · Interested into Catharsis · Distracted into Amazement (level 7).

At higher levels: one more target per slot level above 1, up to 6 targets with a level 6 slot.

features.name: Weave Surge: Sadness
features.bodyHtml:
Weigh a creature down with a grey thread of sorrow.

The target's movement speed is halved, and it can only take either an action or a bonus action. When the surge fades, it leaves the target Pensive for 5 turns, with its movement speed reduced by 3m.

Reacts with: Distracted into Disapproval, Bored into Remorse · Apprehensive into Despair, Annoyed into Envy (level 5) · Accepting into Sentimentality, Interested into Pessimism (level 9) · Serene into Catharsis · Pensive into Grief (level 7).

At higher levels: one more target per slot level above 1, up to 6 targets with a level 6 slot.

features.name: The Two Cups
features.bodyHtml:
Tip every cup in the room at once. Every creature within 18m that carries a mood undergoes Catharsis: enemies take 2d8 Psychic damage and allies regain 2d8 hit points, plus Attunement's extra 1d8. Every mood is spent.

Costs no Woven Spell Slot. You can cast it only while the Aspect of Empathy is awakened (Tier I or higher). Each Catharsis it causes counts towards your next tier.

features.name: Complex Feelings
features.bodyHtml: Emotions two steps apart on the wheel now braid into complex feelings, such as Hope or Despair.

features.name: Weave Surge: Disgust
features.bodyHtml:
Twist a creature's Weave into revulsion.

The target can't take actions and has Disadvantage on Constitution Saving Throws. When the surge fades, it leaves the target Bored for 5 turns, unable to take reactions.

Reacts with: Pensive into Remorse, Annoyed into Contempt · Distracted into Unbelief, Interested into Cynicism (level 5) · Serene into Morbidness, Apprehensive into Shame (level 9) · Accepting into Catharsis · Bored into Loathing (level 7).

At higher levels: one more target per slot level above 1, up to 6 targets with a level 6 slot.

features.name: Weave Surge: Anger
features.bodyHtml:
Set a red thread of fury alight in a creature's mind.

The target attacks the nearest creature other than you. When the surge fades, it leaves the target Annoyed for 5 turns, with its Armour Class reduced by 1.

Reacts with: Bored into Contempt, Interested into Aggressiveness · Serene into Pride, Pensive into Envy (level 5) · Accepting into Dominance, Distracted into Outrage (level 9) · Apprehensive into Catharsis · Annoyed into Rage (level 7).

At higher levels: one more target per slot level above 1, up to 6 targets with a level 6 slot.

features.name: Overwhelm
features.bodyHtml:
A Weave Surge on a creature whose mood echoes the same emotion pulls the thread tight into its overwhelming form, such as Ecstasy or Terror.

The overwhelming emotion lasts 1 turn, then the mood returns for 5 turns. See Overwhelming emotions.

features.name: Turn the Wheel
features.bodyHtml:
Choose a creature that carries a mood and a direction. Its mood turns one step around the wheel, clockwise or anticlockwise: Serene becomes Accepting or Interested, Apprehensive becomes Accepting or Distracted. An enemy can resist with a Wisdom Saving Throw.

Use it to line up the reaction you want before your Surge lands, such as turning a mood into the opposite of the Surge you are about to cast.

features.name: Aspect of Empathy: Tier II
features.bodyHtml: Your Awakening can now reach Tier II, Harmony, after 5 reactions in a fight. See Aspect of Empathy.

features.name: Mixed Feelings
features.bodyHtml: Emotions three steps apart on the wheel now braid into mixed feelings, such as Delight or Shame.

features.name: Emotional Contagion
features.bodyHtml:
Choose a creature that carries an emotion, a mood or a feeling, and one of them spreads. Every other creature within 6m of it catches the same state. Creatures that aren't your allies can resist with a Wisdom Saving Throw.

The copies last while you keep Concentration.

features.name: Ready: Compassion
features.bodyHtml: Until combat ends, when an ally within 9m takes damage, you can use your reaction to cast Weave Surge: Trust on it. The Surge reacts with the ally's mood as usual through Emotional Alchemy.

features.name: Equanimity
features.bodyHtml: Still every cup around you. Allies within 9m lose every hindering emotion, mood and feeling, and are immune to hostile Surges for 3 turns.

features.name: Aspect of Empathy: Tier III
features.bodyHtml: Your Awakening can now reach Tier III after 7 reactions in a fight, and you awaken as the Aspect of Empathy. See Aspect of Empathy.

blocks.html: Temperance awakens through mixing. Every reaction you cause during a fight counts towards your next tier: each feeling you braid, each overwhelming emotion and each Catharsis counts as 1, on allies and enemies alike, and every Catharsis caused by The Two Cups counts separately. Each goal you reach awakens one more tier, and everything lasts until combat ends. Your count shows on the Awakening Progress status.

tiers.label: Tier I · Attunement
itemsHtml: Catharsis deals or restores an additional 1d8.
Moods you create last 2 turns longer.
You can cast The Two Cups.

tiers.label: Tier II · Harmony
itemsHtml: Once per turn, when you braid a feeling, the nearest other creature within 6m gains the mood of one of that feeling's two emotions.

tiers.label: Tier III · Aspect of Empathy
itemsHtml: Your Weave Surges touch one more target.
Every reaction you cause on an ally also grants it temporary hit points.

blocks.title: Pouring for the Aspect
blocks.html: Harmony feeds itself: each feeling you braid leaves a fresh mood on the creature next to it, ready for your next Surge. At Tier III, a Surge cast with a level 6 slot touches 7 creatures, so a single action can braid, overwhelm and snap across half the battlefield.
